_comment: Extra accepted answers for exact-match steps, applied to the generated
Why this exists: checkAnswer.js:176-185 compares answerType 'string'
literally -- parsed = attempt, then _equality, with no normalisation. But
_equality takes an array, so the platform already accepts a list of
correct answers. Only the tooling discards it: create_content.py:265
hardcodes stepAnswer: [answer]. So we supply the list here.
Without this every Data 100 problem is effectively unsolvable: all three
regex answers are stored with literal surrounding backticks, which no
Only list patterns that are genuinely correct for the question. The
script adds backtick- and r""-wrapped forms of each entry automatically.

row2.note: Strip leading zeroes off a room number and capture the rest. Body guarantees no room number is all zeroes.

row4.note: Capture the street name following the street number in '123 San Pablo Ave, 94702'.

row5.note: Course IDs of exactly three digits.

row1.note: Matches of \d+ against 'It has been 71 years since the year 1954.' -- an extraction result, not a pattern. commaSpacing expands the separators.
